headline: Rupee Co-operative Bank: the warning was a blank record, not an early signal
dek: The replay cannot establish that Rupee Co-operative Bank’s balance sheet felt stress first. It establishes a stricter lesson: when liability disclosures and vetted inputs are absent, an institution is outside the lens—not safely inside it.

review_notes: Removed unsupported causal claims about Rupee’s specific balance-sheet path.
Separated filing-period observations, market-price signals, and model derivations.
Retained scoreability, timing, construction-PIT, market-authority, stale-data, and validation limitations.
Added a counter-case that rules out comparative early-warning claims for this institution.

corrections.summary: Three co-operative bank failures in the India crisis record are dated at their onset, the first RBI directions restricting depositors, instead of the later licence cancellation. The India figures were regenerated, and Failure Radar tier publication is paused pending re-validation.
corrections.note: **Correction, 3 November 2026.** LiquiLens now dates three co-operative bank failures in its India crisis record at their onset, the first RBI directions restricting depositors, instead of the later licence cancellation: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank on 13 March 2001 (previously 4 June 2012), CKP Co-operative Bank on 2 May 2014 (previously 30 April 2020) and Rupee Co-operative Bank on 22 February 2013 (previously 22 September 2022). Sources: RBI press releases of [7 June 2012](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=26606), [5 May 2014](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=31124) and [25 February 2013](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=28200). Each bank's only scored filing fell after its onset, so all three are now unscored for insufficient data rather than flagged. This article originally gave 2022-09-22, the day Rupee Co-operative Bank's licence cancellation took effect, as its default date; the text below now gives 2013-02-22. The India figures cited below were regenerated: the share of non-fraud failures flagged moved from 88.9% to 86.7% (13 of 15), and the median lead from 21.5 to 23 months. Failure Radar tiers are now paused pending re-validation. Board states and validation statistics below are as served on the publication date, and the text is otherwise as published.
